To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new screening strategy for complex I mutants in Chlamydomomonas, which is fast and suited to high-throughput screening, and which allowed the identification of a new mutant of the NDUFAF complex.

a) the photosystem II efficiency of Chlamy­domonas mutants defective for complex I can be used for the fast and efficient identification of complex I mutants; b) the photosystem I efficiency of Chlamyd­o­mo­nas mutants defective for complex II can be used for fast and efficient identification for complex II mutants; c) this screening method is suitable for the identification of mutants in the mitochondrial electron transport chain.

a mutant of NDUFAF1, a gene encoding a mitochondrial protein involved in complex I (CI) assembly, was isolated by screening for mutants with a reduced photosystem II (PSII) efficiency in a background of reduced chloroplast CI activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a fast screening method for complex I mutants based on chlorophyll fluorescence measurements and with the characterization of a new complex I mutant in the microalgal Chlamydomonassp. reinhardtii.
the development of a high-throughput screening method based on chlorophyll fluorescence to identify complex I mutants in microalgae.
the development and application of new screening methods for the identification of mutants in the microalgae Chlamydomons reinhardtii, which are deficient for mitochondrial respiratory complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a fast and efficient screening method has been developed for complex I mutants in Chlamydomomonas.

the pgrl-1 mutant is an excellent tool to screen for complex I mutants in Chlamydomonasmicroalga, and that the screening is based on the fact that the pgr1-1 mutation is not able to compensate a complex I mutation, leading to a decrease in the photosynthetic efficiency of the pgr1 complex I mutant.
the screening method is not only fast, but also very efficient, and that this method is particularly suited for the isolation of complex I mutants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photosynthetic pgrl1 mutation is a useful genetic tool to identify Chlamydomas complex I mutants.
the screening method based on the measurement of chlorophyll a fluorescence is a powerful tool for the isolation of Chlamydamonas complex I mutants.
we describe here an efficient screening method to identify mutants defective for complex I assembly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in vivo chlorophyll fluorometry can be used to identify complex I assembly mutants in the micro-algae Chlamydomonassp. reinhardtii.

in Chlamydomonass, the screening method based on photosystem II fluorescence is suitable for the selection of complex I mutants, but the screening method based upon the growth rate under heterotrophic growth is not.

the screening method is not limited to the identification of complex I mutants, but can be used to isolate mutants defective for the assembly of any complex in the mitochondrial electron transport chain, provided that the mutant is defective in the formation of an electrochemical gradient in the organelle.
